findings.text: When the source and target value types differ, mergeMaps only logs and `continue`s, so the new file's value is silently dropped. An explicit `null` (nil type) in the merged file is dropped the same way, and so is `port: "80"` over an existing int `port: 80`. The merge reports success but doesn't override.

For `map[interface{}]interface{}` targets, `stv` is a shallow copy of `ttv`, so writes go to the copy and are mirrored into `ttv` via `itgt` using the string key. If the existing map has non-string keys (e.g. int `1`), the merged key `"1"` doesn't match the original key `1`. A duplicate string key is added next to it instead of overriding it.

In the default branch and the new-key branch, `itgt[sk]` or `itgt[tk]` is written by string key. A case-variant key such as `Foo` versus an existing `foo` can leave two entries that differ only by case in the original `map[interface{}]interface{}`, so lookups may return the stale value.

1.reason: This is the same root cause as the reference bug: mergeMaps uses string keys to write into the original map[interface{}]interface{} via itgt, causing type/key mismatches instead of merging into existing non-string keys.

2.reason: This is also the same root cause: writing by string key into the original map[interface{}]interface{} via itgt can create duplicate case-variant keys instead of merging into the existing key, which is the same mechanism as the reference bug.
